headline: Democrat Roy Cooper flips North Carolina Senate seat, crucial for party's control
summary: Roy Cooper, a former two-term governor, defeated Trump-backed Republican Michael Whatley, marking a significant gain for Democrats in their bid to secure Senate majority. He campaigned on addressing the high cost of food and energy.
details: Democrat Roy Cooper has won North Carolina's US Senate race, according to media projections. He defeated Trump-backed Republican Michael Whatley, securing a crucial pickup for Democrats in their battle for Senate control.

Cooper, a well-known former two-term governor, campaigned on issues like the high cost of food and energy. His victory comes as former President Donald Trump's approval ratings have reportedly fallen.
Before Tuesday's elections, Republicans held a 53-47 Senate majority. Democrats needed a net gain of four seats to take control of the chamber.

The 69-year-old Cooper will replace Republican Senator Thom Tillis, who announced his retirement. Tillis had previously broken with Trump over Medicaid cuts in the president
’s signature tax and spending law.
With strong statewide name recognition, Cooper built a significant polling lead leading up to the election. He garnered substantial support from independent voters across the state.
Michael Whatley, a former Republican National Committee chair, had never held elective office before this race. He campaigned alongside Donald Trump in North Carolina.
In 2024, Trump endorsed Whatley to replace Ronna McDaniel as RNC chair. Alongside Trump's daughter-in-law Lara Trump as co-chair, Whatley led an RNC election integrity drive.
caption:
Democrat Roy Cooper has secured a vital US Senate seat in North Carolina, defeating a Trump-backed Republican. This win is a significant boost for Democrats aiming to control the Senate.

Democrat Roy Cooper has won North Carolina's US Senate race, according to media projections. He defeated Trump-backed Republican Michael Whatley, securing a crucial pickup for Democrats in their battle for Senate control.

Cooper, a well-known former two-term governor, campaigned on issues like the high cost of food and energy. His victory comes as former President Donald Trump's approval ratings have reportedly fallen.

Before Tuesday's elections, Republicans held a 53-47 Senate majority. Democrats needed a net gain of four seats to take control of the chamber.

The 69-year-old Cooper will replace Republican Senator Thom Tillis, who announced his retirement. Tillis had previously broken with Trump over Medicaid cuts in the president
’s signature tax and spending law.

With strong statewide name recognition, Cooper built a significant polling lead leading up to the election. He garnered substantial support from independent voters across the state.

Michael Whatley, a former Republican National Committee chair, had never held elective office before this race. He campaigned alongside Donald Trump in North Carolina.

In 2024, Trump endorsed Whatley to replace Ronna McDaniel as RNC chair. Alongside Trump's daughter-in-law Lara Trump as co-chair, Whatley led an RNC election integrity drive.

headline_marked: [[Indian cricket team agrees to visit Bangladesh]] for a limited-overs series in January
headline: Indian cricket team agrees to visit Bangladesh for a limited-overs series in January
summary: The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) have reportedly agreed in principle for a three-ODI and three-T20I series to be held in the first week of January. This follows ongoing discussions between the two boards.
details: The Indian cricket team is expected to visit Bangladesh in the first week of January for a series comprising three One-Day Internationals (ODIs) and three Twenty20 Internationals (T20Is). This potential tour follows an agreement in principle between the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).

Multiple BCB sources informed Prothom Alo that both boards have agreed to play the series in the first half of January. BCB President Tamim Iqbal expressed optimism, stating, "We are discussing a window. The way our discussions with the BCCI are progressing, I am hopeful that the Indian team will come to Bangladesh to play the series."

Tamim Iqbal updated the BCB working committee on October 28 about the progress of discussions with the BCCI regarding the tour. He indicated that the series could start in the first week of January and conclude by the second week.

Discussions between the two boards have been ongoing, with BCB President Tamim Iqbal holding informal talks with BCCI officials during ICC and ACC meetings. A recent Zoom meeting saw officials from both boards agree in principle to play the series in early January, considering India's busy international schedule.

Beyond the cricket boards' agreement, the tour requires a "green signal" from the governments of both countries due to political relations. Although government permission isn't explicitly part of the BCB-BCCI discussions, both boards acknowledge its necessity.

A BCB official, speaking anonymously, stated, "Since the BCCI is continuing discussions with us and has more or less agreed on the series timing, we assume their government is positive about it. We are also in communication with our government and are receiving positive responses."

BCB President Tamim Iqbal regularly communicates with State Minister for Youth and Sports Aminul Haque regarding the Indian team's visit. Minister Haque affirmed, "We always want to keep sports out of politics. We want friendly relations with neighboring countries to be strengthened."

The Sports Minister confirmed that discussions are underway for a January series, though the exact timing is not yet finalized. A BCB director expressed confidence in BCCI's positive stance, stating, "If they weren't positive, they wouldn't be discussing this, holding Zoom meetings, or finding new dates."

This highly anticipated tour has been scheduled twice before but was postponed each time due to "cold diplomatic relations" between the two countries. The previous postponements highlight the importance of government approval for the series to proceed.

The BCB first announced a schedule for this series on April 15 last year, with India expected in August. Another tentative schedule for September this year was also announced by BCB for its 2026 home series plan, but BCCI never confirmed it, citing international schedule conflicts.
